subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw enforce automatic sensitive-value sanitization on final agent outputs in core, route it to a plugin using existing hooks, or keep core limited to current log/tool/transcript redaction boundaries?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the requested behavior defines a security boundary and visible output policy that can change final replies, channel delivery, tool payload exposure, configuration defaults, and false-positive handling.

options.title: Approve a narrow core security design
options.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core sanitizer with schema, docs, tests, reporting, and delivery-surface coverage before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Treat this as optional output policy implemented by a code plugin, adding core SDK seams only if the plugin proves a missing API.

options.title: Keep current core boundary
options.body: Document logs, transcripts, tool payloads, diagnostics, and UI safety surfaces as the supported core redaction boundary and split or close final-output requests only after that decision.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core security design
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in or explicitly scoped core sanitizer with schema, docs, tests, reporting, and delivery-surface coverage before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice defines a security-sensitive output boundary and intersects CODEOWNERS security/config/secrets ownership.
